# 1 Enoch Chapter 16 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 16 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 16:1 — Structure of the complex opening sentence

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Single complex participial sentence | Preserves the Ge'ez syntactic structure |
| LOGOS | Single complex sentence with em-dash clarification | Clarifies the participial phrase while preserving the sentence unity |
| PNEUMA | Broken into two sentences | 'From the time...up until...' / 'That judgment will fall...' — prioritizes readability |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS single complex sentence. The syntactic complexity of v. 1 is part of the divine speech's formal register. Breaking it up (PNEUMA) makes it more accessible but loses the sense that this is a single divine pronouncement covering a vast temporal scope.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 16:3 — 'worthless ones' for the mysteries they knew

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "worthless-ones" | Preserves the Ge'ez adjective describing the lesser mysteries |
| LOGOS | "the worthless ones" | Same; the definite article clarifies these are specific mysteries |
| PNEUMA | "the lesser, worthless ones" | Adds 'lesser' as an explanatory gloss |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS 'the worthless ones.' PNEUMA's 'lesser, worthless ones' is an interpretive gloss that goes beyond the text. The Ge'ez text says 'worthless' (or 'useless') mysteries — meaning mysteries of no ultimate value — without the comparative 'lesser.'

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 16:4 — Final verdict: 'You have no peace' vs. 'You shall have no peace'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "You-have-no-peace" | Present tense; the verdict is already in effect |
| LOGOS | "You shall have no peace" | Future tense; the verdict extends forward |
| PNEUMA | "You will have no peace" | Future tense; modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'You shall have no peace' (LOGOS). The consistent use of future 'shall' for the judgment-refrain throughout the Book of Watchers (chs. 5, 12, 13) is important for the echo-effect. All three translators agree on the substance.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS for consistency with established refrain.

---

## Overall assessment

Chapter 16 is a brief four-verse conclusion to the divine speech, largely straightforward. Total significant divergences: 3. Key areas: sentence structure of v. 1, the description of the mysteries in v. 3, and the verb tense of the final verdict.
